newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end sharply lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended sharply lower as end-of-month buying failed to emerge following the morning's frantic sell-off, traders said.
"I would have expected to see more of a bid come into the market," one Standard & Poor's 500 futures trader said.
While short-covering was noted, there was little buying momentum to prod the September S&P contract much above the 653.00 level for the rest of the afternoon.
"You would have thought there would be a little bit of dough being put to work here," another S&P floor source said as September languished around 652.00.
However, Jay Hohmann, head of stock index futures at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, said chart patterns suggest cash S&P 500s will test and surpass their highs.
"I've got a renewed bullishness," he said. "The Dow Industrials going to 6,000 by the end of the year is not impossible."
Hohmann said the low 650.00 handle in cash S&Ps represented a pivot point, but that the index could drop to 640.00 and still manage to rebound.
"This is the zone where the market went steaming through," he said. "There is a level of support here."
One futures trader pegged support for September at 648.00, and said a violation of that level could lead the contract to the low 640.00s.

The August National Association of Purchasing Management index for the Chicago region rose to 60.0, from 51.2 in July. The increase was the largest monthly rise since December 1993, and the highest level since 62.6 in February 1995.
The report, coupled with an increase in July U.S. factory orders and in the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment survey, pressured U.S. stocks lower.
The data suggested that inflationary pressures may start creeping up in the U.S. economy in the third quarter, thereby disproving forecasts of a U.S. economic slowdown sometime in the year.

Fair value for September was at 0.95 point to cash. Arbitrage buy programs were noted in the first two hours of trade at about 1.30 points over cash. Arbitrage sell programs were reportedly 0.20 under.
U.S. markets will be closed on Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday.

At the end of pit trade, September S&Ps were off 5.80 at 651.35, NYSE New Composites off 2.20 at 350.95, KBT Value Lines off 1.60 at 616.70, Nikkeis down 325 at 20,185, Midcaps off 0.20 at 232.45 and Nasdaqs off 6.80 at 665.40.
